name: Zanga
description: Zanga is a Spanish trick-taking game related to Hombre/Tresillo. 4 players in 2 teams. 32-card Spanish deck. 8 each. Permanent trumps: Ace of Swords (highest), Ace of Clubs, King of Clubs. Trump chooser's team must win 5+ tricks. Winning all = bonus. Extra points for holding top 3+ trumps.

history.origins: Zanga is a four-player card game and a relative of Hombre and Tresillo. It is played in Spain in the region north of Malaga (Cuenca del Río Campanillas), in villages such as Villanueva de la Concepción, Almogía and Campanillas, and is also popular in the Canary Islands. The Malaga version uses a 32-card Spanish pack; the Canary Islands version uses the full 40-card pack with Tresillo-style ranking.
timeline: Regional tradition: played in Spain north of Malaga (Cuenca del Río Campanillas) and in the Canary Islands; Hombre/Tresillo relative.

setup.players: Four players in two fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite each other.
setup.deck: 32-card Spanish deck (40-card in Canary Islands version). Eight cards per player in the Malaga 32-card version.
setup.dealing: Eight cards are dealt to each player from the 32-card pack (Malaga version); ten each in the 40-card Canary Islands version.

rules.objective: The partnership that chooses trumps must win at least five of the eight tricks to score. If they take only four tricks they lose (puesta); if three or fewer they lose more (codillo). Bonuses for winning all tricks, holding the top three trumps, or winning the first five.
rules.gameplay: Permanent trumps: A♠(Swords)=highest, A♣, K♣. Choose trump suit. Must win 5+ tricks. All 8 = bonus. Holding top 3+ trumps = extra points. Failure = puesta/codillo penalty.

variations.emptyOverridesReason: No named variants documented in sources; Malaga vs Canary deck differ but not modeled as overrides yet.

scoring.description: Points for meeting trick quota. Bonuses for sweep and top trumps.
